This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') has been filed challenging the award dated 19/03/2022 passed in claim case No.133/2022 by the 3rd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rajnandgaon, (CG) (for short 'Tribunal').

entities.text: 3rd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rajnandgaon
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By the impugned award, against a claim of Rs.60,00,000/-, learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.18,66,000/- in favour of the appellants / claimants.

2. The claim application under Section 166 of the MV Act has been filed on account of death of Mukund Patel in an accident that occurred on 19/03/2022 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Car) bearing registration No.CG 07 BF 6750 by respondent No.1, owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3.
As per pleadings of the claim application, the deceased was aged about 35 years and was a carpenter.
Therefore, the aforestated compensation was claimed.
3. The respondents 1 and 2 filed written statement and denied averments of the claim application.

The insurance company except admitted facts denied averments of the claim application and took a plea that there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy as and the driver was not having valid and effective driving license.
4.
On the basis of above pleadings, learned Claims Tribunal framed issues and decided the same in favour of the appellants / claimants and awarded the abovestated compensation.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income of the deceased has wrongly been assessed.
Therefore, the compensation may be enhanced.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 submits that just compensation has been awarded.
Therefore, no interference with the award is warranted.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.
8.

Taking into consideration the age, dependency, minimum wages etc., this Court assesses the monthly income of the deceased to Rs.11,000/- and taking guidance from the judgments of Hon'ble Smt Rajmat Bai Patel vs Shiv Kumar on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80897003/

The learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.18,66,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation now assessed and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.3,44,400/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of appeal i.e. 05/02/2024 to be deposited by the insurance company within a period of 60 days.
